checks.s: The memo identifies the exclusivity provision (Article 3) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft grants sole exclusivity for 24 months post-award or 18 months post-solicitation close if no award.
The memo notes the playbook requires co-exclusive only with a maximum 6 months post-proposal submission if no award.
The memo recommends revising exclusivity to co-exclusive status.
The memo recommends capping the no-award exclusivity tail at 6 months post-proposal submission.

The memo notes that the draft's broad/lengthy exclusivity contradicts the parties' preliminary understanding of mutual exclusivity limited to the JTCP solicitation only (per the teaming discussion notes).
The memo identifies the non-compete provision (Article 4) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft prohibits VDS from teaming on any 'tactical communications' opportunity with any other prime.
The memo notes the playbook requires limitation of the non-compete to solicitation W15QKN-25-R-0412 only.
The memo notes that broad market-based non-competes are playbook-designated walk-away terms.
The memo recommends narrowing the non-compete scope to solicitation W15QKN-25-R-0412 only.
The memo identifies the workshare commitment (Article 5) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft uses 'commercially reasonable efforts' with no binding workshare percentage.
The memo notes the playbook requires a binding minimum workshare percentage with ±3% tolerance.
The memo recommends inserting a binding 28% workshare commitment.
The memo recommends a ±3% tolerance on the binding workshare commitment.
The memo identifies the foreground IP assignment (Article 8) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft assigns all foreground IP developed 'in connection with' the teaming arrangement to Apex.
The memo notes the playbook requires jointly owned or developing-party owned IP with a license for contract performance only.
The memo recommends revising foreground IP to developing-party ownership with a performance-only license to the other party.
The memo identifies the background IP license (Article 8) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes that perpetual/irrevocable background IP licenses are playbook-designated walk-away terms.
The memo notes the draft grants Apex a royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable license to VDS background IP.
The memo notes the playbook requires a no-transfer, limited, revocable license for proposal preparation and contract performance only.
The memo specifically addresses the risk to VDS's Spectra-Link SDR architecture in the background IP analysis.
The memo notes Spectra-Link is VDS's core competitive asset developed entirely at private expense.
The memo notes Spectra-Link carries limited rights/restricted rights DFARS classifications and/or pending patent applications.
The memo notes that the parties previously discussed VDS retention of all Spectra-Link background IP with only a limited performance license to Apex, per the teaming discussion notes.
The memo identifies the subcontract obligation (Article 7) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft uses permissive 'may' language with no timing requirement and full flow-down without negotiation.
The memo notes the playbook requires mandatory 'shall' language with a 60-day deadline and a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit.
The memo recommends revising Article 7 to mandatory 'shall' language with a 60-day post-award deadline.
The memo recommends adding a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit.
The memo identifies the termination for convenience clause (Article 12) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft grants Apex-only termination on 10 days' notice with no reciprocal VDS right and no B&P cost reimbursement.
The memo notes the playbook requires a mutual right with 30 days' notice and documented B&P cost reimbursement if terminated pre-award.
The memo recommends making termination for convenience mutual.
The memo recommends extending the termination notice period to 30 days.
The memo recommends adding B&P cost reimbursement.
The memo identifies the liability cap (Article 14) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft caps liability at $250,000 per party.
The memo notes the playbook requires the greater of $2,000,000 or 2× the workshare value under any issued task order.
The memo notes that given VDS's estimated $45.27M workshare the $250K cap is grossly inadequate.
The memo recommends revising the liability cap to the greater of $2,000,000 or 2× the task-order workshare value.
The memo identifies the indemnification provision (Article 13) as a HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft imposes one-sided indemnification (VDS indemnifies Apex for all third-party IP claims, with no reciprocal indemnity).
The memo notes the playbook requires mutual and symmetrical IP infringement indemnification.
The memo recommends revising indemnification to mutual and symmetrical.
The memo identifies the dispute resolution clause (Article 15) as a MEDIUM risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft provides binding arbitration under AAA rules with a single arbitrator in Reston, VA, with no injunctive relief carve-out.
The memo notes the playbook's escalation ladder (negotiation → mediation → litigation in E.D. Va.) with injunctive relief preserved.
The memo recommends replacing binding arbitration with the playbook's negotiation → mediation → litigation (Eastern District of Virginia) escalation ladder.
The memo recommends adding an injunctive relief carve-out.
The memo identifies the ITAR/export control provision (Article 10) as a MEDIUM or HIGH risk deviation.
The memo notes the draft places sole responsibility on VDS for all export control compliance.
The memo notes the playbook requires mutual obligation with each party responsible for its own data and a joint compliance protocol exhibit.
The memo recommends revising Article 10 to mutual ITAR/export obligations.
The memo recommends adding a joint compliance protocol exhibit.
The memo identifies the absence of a protest/award challenge cooperation clause as a MEDIUM risk missing protection.
The memo notes the playbook requires mutual cooperation if a GAO or COFC protest is filed.
The memo recommends adding a protest/award challenge cooperation clause.
The memo identifies the absence of VDS key personnel protections as a MEDIUM risk missing protection.
The memo notes Exhibit C lists only Apex-designated key personnel.
The memo notes the playbook requires named VDS key personnel protected from reassignment without VDS consent.
The memo recommends adding VDS key personnel to Exhibit C with consent-to-reassign protections.
The memo identifies the absence of a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit as a MEDIUM risk missing protection.
The memo links the missing pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit to Article 7's permissive subcontract obligation.
The memo recommends attaching a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit.
The memo identifies the absence of a joint ITAR/export compliance protocol exhibit as a missing protection.
The memo recommends adding a joint ITAR/export compliance protocol exhibit consistent with the playbook and VDS standard form.
The memo notes that the draft's exclusivity deviates from the preliminary understanding of mutual exclusivity limited to the JTCP solicitation only (per teaming discussion notes).
The memo highlights this exclusivity deviation as negotiation leverage.
The memo notes that the draft's non-binding workshare deviates from the preliminary understanding that 28% workshare was discussed as a binding commitment.
The memo highlights this workshare deviation as negotiation leverage.

The memo notes that the draft's perpetual/irrevocable background IP license deviates from the preliminary understanding that VDS would retain Spectra-Link background IP with only a limited performance license.
The memo notes that the draft's permissive 'may' subcontract language deviates from the preliminary understanding that subcontract issuance would be mandatory upon award.
The memo notes VDS's small business status.
The memo notes the solicitation's ≥35% small business subcontracting goal.
The memo states that VDS's 28% workshare contributes significantly toward the ≥35% goal, strengthening VDS's negotiating position on the binding workshare commitment.
The memo assigns a risk rating (High/Medium/Low) to every identified deviation.

The memo's risk ratings follow the playbook methodology: High for walk-away or material financial/legal exposure items, Medium for significant deviations requiring negotiation, and Low for minor or cosmetic deviations.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 3 revising exclusivity to co-exclusive.
The redline caps the no-award exclusivity tail at 6 months post-proposal submission.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 4 narrowing the non-compete to solicitation W15QKN-25-R-0412 only.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 5 replacing 'commercially reasonable efforts' with a binding 28% workshare commitment.
The redline includes a ±3% tolerance for the workshare commitment.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 8 (foreground IP) revising to developing-party ownership with a performance-only license.

The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 8 (background IP) replacing the perpetual/irrevocable license with a limited, revocable license for proposal preparation and contract performance only.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 7 changing 'may' to 'shall'.
The redline adds a 60-day post-award deadline for subcontract issuance.
The redline references a pre-negotiated subcontract terms exhibit.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 12 making termination for convenience mutual.
The redline extends the termination notice period to 30 days.
The redline adds B&P cost reimbursement.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 14 revising the liability cap from $250,000 to the greater of $2,000,000 or 2× task-order workshare value.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 13 making indemnification mutual and symmetrical.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 15 replacing binding arbitration with the playbook's escalation ladder (negotiation → mediation → litigation in E.D. Va.).
The redline adds an injunctive relief carve-out.
The redline includes proposed markup language for Article 10 revising to mutual ITAR obligations.
The redline references a joint compliance protocol exhibit.
The redline includes a new provision for mutual protest/award challenge cooperation covering GAO or COFC protests.
The redline adds VDS key personnel to Exhibit C or the key personnel provisions with consent-to-reassign protections.
The redline adds or references a new exhibit for pre-negotiated subcontract terms.
The redline adds or references a new exhibit for a joint ITAR compliance protocol.
The redline adds or references a new exhibit for VDS key personnel protections.
The memo notes that Article 8's foreground IP clause uses the expansive phrase 'in connection with' the teaming arrangement.
The memo notes the 'in connection with' phrase could sweep in pre-existing VDS developments and work outside the JTCP program.
The memo recommends narrowing the foreground IP scope to IP developed solely in performance of the specific subcontract.
The memo notes that the 'in connection with' language risks capturing modifications or enhancements to Spectra-Link.
The memo notes Spectra-Link is used across multiple VDS programs.
The memo notes that VDS's Spectra-Link data qualifies as 'limited rights' technical data under DFARS 252.227-7013.
The memo notes that VDS's Spectra-Link software qualifies as 'restricted rights' computer software under DFARS 252.227-7014.
The memo notes that the draft's perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free background IP license to Apex is inconsistent with these DFARS protections.
The redline markup of Article 8 (background IP) references or incorporates DFARS 252.227-7013 and/or -7014 protections for VDS's limited rights/restricted rights data.
The memo is addressed to Nathaniel R. Chu (General Counsel, VDS).
The memo references engagement number LHR-2025-0743.
The memo references or is dated in relation to the July 18, 2025 deadline.

The memo notes that the mutual consequential damages waiver (Article 14) could prevent VDS from recovering lost profits if Apex fails to issue a binding subcontract or terminates, putting the $45.27M workshare at risk.
The memo recommends carving out lost workshare value from the consequential damages waiver or tying it to the revised liability cap.
Each deviation entry in the memo identifies the specific article/section of the Apex draft.
Each deviation entry states the corresponding playbook requirement.
Each deviation entry describes the nature of the deviation.
Each deviation entry carries a risk rating (High/Medium/Low).
Each deviation entry includes a recommended negotiation position with fallback options.
The memo flags that Article 7 states full flow-down 'without negotiation'.
The memo recommends pre-negotiated subcontract terms with appropriate tailoring.
The memo addresses the mixed FFP/CPFF task order structure of the IDIQ in connection with the flow-down/subcontract terms recommendation.
